items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The band was under the leadership of Benny Carter but I dont remember who the other members were except Cour//ance and Mack Horton on trombone.

ctx.x: The most embarrassing gig I ever went on was a pick up band that played in Atlantic city under the name of Duke Ellington. This must have happened around 31 or 32 and I made the trip with "Spider" Caurance who still had the same model 'T' Ford that he had bought before I left Wes Helvey around 1926. Spider had old types onthe car, and it was a very hot day when we left New York.

He must have had 10 blow outs and the inkertubes had more patches on them than flies in ano open sugar barrel. I thought we'd never make it to Atlantic City on time but we did. The dance was on the pier in a place that was usually reserved for the white public but this night, it was for a Negro dance. The band was under the leadership of Benny Carter but I dont remember who the other members were except Cour//ance and Mack Horton on trombone.

We got on the bandstand and after a couple of numbers, some cats standing close to the bandstand who knew the personnel of Duke's orchestra started asking very loudly: "Where is Johnny Hodges? Where is Freddie Jenkins? Where is Barney Bigard?' and so on... When Fletcher Henderson had a pick up band playing under his name in New Jersey, he did come on the gig and direct the musicians for a while, but Duke was in New York at the Cotton Club and no one in the orchestra resembled Duke. What an embarrassing night.....
